graphEvents.label: A 218-byte comments directive is 71 percent of the median brief
Identical brief bytes but 0 of 10 to 7 of 10 start-policy starts
What does the brief wording cost a model that would start a workflow

label: Every brief ends with a fixed 218-byte tail, a 12-byte label plus a 206-byte comment-hygiene directive, which is 71 percent of the 306-byte median live brief.
The command line is about 13 percent of a median brief: a 39-byte label for system-deep-loop to deep-review plus about 15 bytes of scores and pass.
The policy word is printed but never defined; the brief has no legend for run, start or ask, and the only explanatory block is the hygiene directive.
At identical brief bytes the on-arm start-policy starts are Claude 0 of 10, OpenCode 5 of 10, pi 4 of 10, devin 5 of 10 and dsh 7 of 10, so wording cannot cause the spread.
Claude started none of its ten start-policy rows in either arm and capped none, so the advisor-on gain came from run or ask rows.
The ask word does not reliably produce an ask: on the five ask-policy rows the on arm started 1 on Claude, 0 on OpenCode, 0 on pi, 2 on devin and 3 on dsh.
The head is not truncated in practice: an 80-token cap is about 320 characters against an 88-byte median head, so the command and policy always fit.

Inference: a brief whose last sentence is an unrelated HARD BLOCK about code comments spends the reader's final attention on a rule that cannot help it act on the command; an A/B with the tail moved or removed would confirm it.

reason: The 80-token cap is far above the 88-byte measured head, so the command and policy always fit.
